title: Cell Death, Atomic Biophysics & Physiology
subtitle: Deep Dive Audio Series • Shoulders of Giants, Patch-Clamp Biophysics, Ferroptosis & 1-Angstrom Molecular Machines

sections.heading: Shoulders of Giants: Cellular Energetics, Receptors & Second Messengers

episodes.label: Windows, Workloads, and Diffusing Gas — Ambulatory ECG Cadence & EMBRACE/CRYSTAL AF Trials (H041), Exercise Stress Physiology, HRR & ISCHEMIA (H042) & Plethysmographic Lung Volumes & DLCO/KCO (H043)
episodes.notes: Clinical Cluster & Cardiopulmonary Physiology synthesis of ambulatory ECG monitoring (H041), cardiac exercise stress testing (H042), and lung volumes/DLCO (H043): Barrett's paired patch cohort (n=146), EMBRACE (n=572) & CRYSTAL AF (n=441), nocturnal vagal variants, and toothbrush pseudo-VT; coronary autoregulation, ST localization laws, LBBB vasodilator rule, Cole's HRR (n=2,428), WOMEN & ISCHEMIA; and Boyle's Law plethysmography vs. gas dilution, Roughton-Forster DLCO/KCO physics, CPFE/PAH phenotypes, ppo-DLCO, and race-neutral GLI Z-scores.

episodes.label: The Drug That Took the Long Way — Parkinson's Vallecular Tablet Retention on Videofluoroscopy, Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC Gut Decarboxylation & Oral vs. Jejunal Levodopa-Carbidopa Gel Kinetics
episodes.notes: Mechanical and microbial bottlenecks along levodopa's route from mouth to brain: videofluoroscopic discovery of tablet retention in the valleculae (Sato et al. 2018), carbidopa-insensitive gut microbial tyrosine decarboxylase (Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC) and Eggerthella lenta dopamine dehydroxylase (Maini Rekdal et al. 2019; van Kessel et al. 2019), and oral vs. continuous jejunal infusion pharmacokinetics (Othman et al. 2015).

episodes.label: The Breath Before the Heat — Rising End-Tidal CO2 Before Hyperthermia, Skeletal Muscle RyR1 Calcium Leak, Dantrolene Channel Stabilization & Post-Crisis IVCT/CHCT vs. RYR1 Genetic Testing
episodes.notes: Intraoperative malignant hyperthermia from capnography to channel biophysics: why rising end-tidal carbon dioxide precedes core temperature elevation, uncontrolled skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor (RyR1) sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release, dantrolene sodium stabilization of RyR1, and post-crisis workup integrating RYR1 variant sequencing with caffeine-halothane contracture testing.

episodes.label: The Blood That Would Not Turn Red — Acquired Methemoglobinemia (SpO2 86% vs. PaO2 85 mmHg), Multi-Wavelength Co-Oximetry, NADPH Reductase & G6PD Methylene Blue Hemolysis
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into acquired methemoglobinemia and antidote mechanics: why dual-wavelength pulse oximetry locks near 85–86% despite high dissolved arterial PaO2, multi-wavelength co-oximetry separation of ferric (Fe3+) methemoglobin, how methylene blue uses NADPH methemoglobin reductase as an artificial electron shuttle, and why G6PD deficiency converts methylene blue into a trigger for acute Heinz-body hemolysis (Mathiyalagan et al. 2025; ProvayBlue US label).

episodes.label: The Signal That Outlasted the Cigarette — Exhaled CO vs. Urine Cotinine & Anabasine on Nicotine Patch, Langley's Receptor Concept, Human alpha4-beta2 nAChR Varenicline Cryo-EM (6UR8) & the EAGLES Trial
episodes.notes: From John Newport Langley's 1905 'receptive substance' to transplant tobacco abstinence verification: human alpha4-beta2 nAChR cryo-EM structure bound to varenicline (PDB 6UR8), cytisine-to-varenicline partial agonist design, CYP2A6 nicotine-to-cotinine kinetics, LC-MS/MS separation of isobaric nicotine and minor tobacco alkaloid anabasine (m/z 163), and the 8,144-participant EAGLES trial.

episodes.label: The Flush That Fooled the Numbers — Extended-Release Niacin vs. Nicotinamide, Goldberger's Pellagra, HCAR2/GPR109A Cryo-EM (8IJA), Langerhans PGD2/DP1 Flushing & AIM-HIGH/HPS2-THRIVE Trial Futility
episodes.notes: From pellagra prevention to the HDL surrogate fallacy: nicotinic acid vs. nicotinamide chemistry, human HCAR2/GPR109A cryo-EM structure bound to niacin (PDB 8IJA), Langerhans-cell and keratinocyte PGD2/DP1 flushing vs. laropiprant blockade, glycine-conjugation vs. amidation metabolic saturation, and the AIM-HIGH and HPS2-THRIVE cardiovascular outcome trials.

episodes.label: The Channel That Wouldn't Let Calcium Through — Extended-Release Verapamil Overdose, Fleckenstein's Calcium Antagonism, Rabbit CaV1.1 Cryo-EM (6JPA), Beta-Cell Hyperglycemia & High-Dose Insulin Therapy
episodes.notes: From Albrecht Fleckenstein's discovery of calcium antagonism to critical-care toxicology: rabbit CaV1.1 cryo-EM structure bound to (S)-verapamil in two central-cavity poses (PDB 6JPA), AV-nodal conduction block, pancreatic beta-cell L-type channel blockade producing diagnostic hyperglycemia, stereoselective CYP3A4 clearance, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy, and EXTRIP non-dialyzability.

episodes.label: The Dose That Bought Another Hour — Parkinson's Levodopa Wearing-Off Diaries, Catechol-O-Methyltransferase (COMT) Mg2+ Coordination (PDB 7XGI), Opicapone Erythrocyte Kinetics, BIPARK-I & Tolcapone Hepatotoxicity
episodes.notes: From Parkinson's wearing-off diaries to peripheral COMT inhibition: separating seated motor OFF time from orthostatic hypotension, competing AADC and COMT metabolic pathways, rat soluble COMT crystal structure bound to opicapone and Mg2+ (PDB 7XGI), plasma LC-MS/MS vs. sustained erythrocyte COMT inhibition kinetics, BIPARK-I/II trial endpoints, and tolcapone vs. opicapone hepatic safety.

episodes.label: The Reference Sample Had Changed — Post-Transplant Forensic DNA Chimerism Across Blood (100% Donor), Buccal Swabs (Mixed Leukocyte Infiltration) & Hair/Eyebrow Follicles
episodes.notes: Forensic genetics of biological chimerism after allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation: why blood reference samples convert completely to the donor's STR and amelogenin sex profile, why buccal swabs yield variable donor-recipient DNA mixtures due to mucosal leukocyte trafficking, and why hair shafts and eyebrow follicles remain reliable recipient reference tissues (Jacewicz et al. 2013; Li et al. 2014; 2026 eyebrow follicle study).

episodes.label: The Rhythm That Waited for the Treadmill — CPVT Exercise Stress ECG (H042), Post-Exertional Bidirectional VT, RYR2 Diastolic Calcium Leak & Paired-Test Repeatability
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H042) investigation of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT): why resting ECGs and structural echocardiography are normal, how adrenergic surge and early post-exercise recovery unmask beat-to-beat alternating bidirectional ventricular tachycardia (Akiba et al. 2026), RYR2 diastolic Ca2+ leak and NCX1 delayed afterdepolarizations (Steinberg et al. 2023), and exercise-test repeatability limits (Peltenburg et al. 2023).

episodes.label: The Movement After the Missing Breath — Video-Polysomnography (H044), Obstructive Sleep Apnea Arousal Pseudo-RBD vs. True REM Sleep Without Atonia & CPAP Resolution
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H044) investigation of nocturnal dream-enactment mimics: how synchronized video-polysomnography (EEG, EOG, submental/limb EMG, nasal pressure, and thoracoabdominal effort belts) separates true alpha-synucleinopathy REM sleep behavior disorder (sustained/phasic REM sleep without atonia) from severe obstructive sleep apnea respiratory-arousal pseudo-RBD that resolves completely on CPAP (Deguchi et al. 2021; Bergmann et al. 2024).

episodes.label: How a Nerve Test Finds Where a Signal Slows — Helmholtz's 1850 Two-Point Subtraction, Hodes's 1948 Human CMAP Velocity, Simpson/Gilliatt Focal Wrist Latency & Ring-Finger Comparison
episodes.notes: Electrophysiology of clinical nerve conduction studies (H045): Helmholtz's (1850) two-point latency subtraction canceling synaptic and contractile delay, Hodes, Larrabee & German's (1948) percutaneous human compound muscle action potential (CMAP) conduction velocity method, Simpson (1956) and Gilliatt & Sears's (1958) localization of focal median nerve entrapment across the carpal tunnel, and Uncini et al.'s (1989) ring-finger median-vs-ulnar internal control.

episodes.label: How a Test Maps Vision Away from Where You're Looking — Goldmann's 1945 Hemispherical Kinetic Bowl, Heijl & Krakau's 1975 Automated Blind-Spot Fixation & 20/20 Chiasmal Hemianopia
episodes.notes: Psychophysics and neuro-ophthalmic anatomy of visual field perimetry: Goldmann's (1945) standardized luminance hemispherical bowl and kinetic target-velocity reaction-time artifact, Heijl & Krakau's (1975) automated computerized static threshold perimetry and blind-spot catch trials, and Ogra et al.'s (2014) proof that optic chiasm compression routinely produces bitemporal visual field loss despite 6/6 (20/20) foveal acuity.

episodes.label: How an Electrode Learned to Measure Glucose — Clark & Lyons's 1962 Enzyme Membrane Electrode, Updike & Hicks's 1967 Dual-Cathode Differential Sensor & Basu's 2013 Interstitial Lag
episodes.notes: Electrochemical and physiological foundations of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM): Clark & Lyons's (1962) enzyme-membrane electrode concept, Updike & Hicks's (1967) dual-cathode active-vs-inactivated polyacrylamide 'enzyme electrode' canceling ambient oxygen drift, subcutaneous interstitial fluid sensing and electroactive drug interference, and Basu et al.'s (2013) human tracer microdialysis proof of physiological capillary-to-interstitial glucose lag.

episodes.label: What a Bright Spot on a PET Scan Is Made Of — Sokoloff's 1977 [14C]Deoxyglucose Hexokinase Trap, Reivich & Phelps's 1979 Human [18F]FDG-PET & Kubota's 1992 Macrophage Microautoradiography
episodes.notes: Biochemical basis and diagnostic specificity of [18F]FDG-PET (H022): Sokoloff et al.'s (1977) hexokinase metabolic trapping of 2-deoxyglucose-6-phosphate, Reivich & Phelps's (1979) human positron emission tomography translation, Som et al.'s (1980) oncologic uptake, and Kubota et al.'s (1992) cellular microautoradiography proving why activated macrophages and granulation tissue generate intense FDG avidity indistinguishable from cancer on a single SUV number.

episodes.label: How a Sleep Study Tells Why Breathing Stopped — Gastaut's 1965 Simultaneous EEG/Airflow/Effort Recording, Sullivan's 1981 Nasal CPAP Pneumatic Splint & PSG vs. Home Testing Denominators
episodes.notes: Historical physiology of polysomnography and sleep-disordered breathing (H044): Gastaut, Tassinari & Duron's (1965–1966) polygraphic separation of obstructive, central, and mixed apneas by comparing airflow against thoracoabdominal effort, Sullivan et al.'s (1981) nasal CPAP pneumatic splint experiment, and the denominator divergence between EEG-verified total sleep time in polysomnography and recording/monitoring time in home sleep apnea testing (Bianchi & Goparaju 2017).

episodes.label: Why a Pinhole Can Sharpen a Blurry Letter — Snellen's 5-Arcminute Optotypes, Bailey-Lovie LogMAR Charts, Campbell & Gregory's 2 mm Aperture & Eagan's Retinal-Illumination Trap
episodes.notes: Physiological optics of clinical visual acuity and refraction (H051): Snellen's (1862) 5-arcminute optotype standard, Bailey & Lovie's (1976) proportional logMAR chart design, Campbell & Gregory's (1960) tradeoff between geometrical blur circles and diffraction across pupil diameters, Eagan et al.'s (1999) demonstration of pinhole retinal-dimming pseudoworsening in maculopathy, and Donders (1864) / Sankaridurg et al. (2017) on cycloplegic vs. non-cycloplegic refraction.

episodes.label: How a Brain Recording Can Reveal a Response Without Movement — Owen's 2006 Tennis/Navigation fMRI Imagery, Sitt's 2014 EEG Complexity Markers & Claassen (2019) / Bodien (2024) Cognitive Motor Dissociation
episodes.notes: Detecting covert command-following in behaviorally unresponsive brain-injured patients: Owen et al.'s (2006) fMRI mental-imagery paradigm, Sitt et al.'s (2014) quantitative EEG markers in disorders of consciousness, Claassen et al.'s (2019) bedside motor-command EEG classifier identifying cognitive motor dissociation and predicting 1-year functional recovery, and Bodien et al.'s (2024) six-center cohort quantifying both prevalence (25%) and negative-result sensitivity limits.

episodes.label: How a Newborn Hearing Screen Listens for an Answer — Jewett & Williston's 1971 Averaged ABR Waves, David Kemp's 1978 Outer-Hair-Cell Otoacoustic Emissions & Starr's 1996 Auditory Neuropathy Paradox
episodes.notes: Objective physiological hearing screening without behavioral responses: Jewett & Williston's (1971) time-locked signal averaging of microvolt auditory brainstem responses (ABR), David Kemp's (1978) discovery of active cochlear outer-hair-cell otoacoustic emissions (OAE), NICU screening validation (Stevens et al. 1990), and Starr et al.'s (1996) discovery of auditory neuropathy with preserved OAEs and absent ABR.

episodes.label: How a Sealed Booth Measures the Air Left in Your Lungs — Hutchinson's 1846 Vital Capacity Spirometer, DuBois's 1956 Boyle's-Law Body Plethysmograph & Trapped Emphysematous Gas vs. Helium Dilution
episodes.notes: From Hutchinson's 1846 spirometer to DuBois's 1956 body plethysmograph (H043): why standard spirometry cannot measure residual volume, applying Boyle's pressure-volume law across a closed airway shutter inside a sealed cabin, and why plethysmography captures non-communicating bullae and trapped emphysematous gas missed by single-breath helium dilution (Bedell et al. 1956; O'Donnell et al. 2010).

episodes.label: How a Treadmill ECG Tests the Heart Under Load — Master's 1929 Two-Step Test, Bellet's 1961 Radio-Telemetry Exercise Recording, Bruce's 1963 Multistage Treadmill Protocol & the Duke Treadmill Score
episodes.notes: From two-step challenges to multistage exercise stress testing (H042): Master & Oppenheimer's (1929) standardized step workload, Bellet et al.'s (1961) radiotelemetry during exercise vs. recovery, Bruce et al.'s (1963) graded multistage treadmill protocol, and Mark et al.'s (1987, 1991) Duke treadmill score integrating exercise time, ST deviation, and symptoms.

episodes.label: How an Eye-Pressure Test Reads Through the Cornea — Schiøtz Indentation, Goldmann & Schmidt's 1957 3.06-mm Applanation Tear-Film & Corneal Stiffness Balance, Ehlers's Cannulated Eye Study & OHTS Corneal Thickness
episodes.notes: Biomechanics of intraocular pressure measurement through the cornea (H052): Schiøtz (1905) indentation vs. Goldmann & Schmidt's (1957) small-area 3.06-mm applanation balancing tear-film capillarity against corneal stiffness, Ehlers et al.'s (1975) direct intracameral manometry demonstrating corneal thickness bias, and OHTS (2002) risk stratification.

episodes.label: How One Breath Tests Gas Transfer — Marie Krogh's 1915 Paired Breath Samples, Ogilvie & Forster's 1957 Helium-Dilution Single-Breath DLCO & Roughton-Forster Membrane vs. Red-Cell Partitioning
episodes.notes: From Marie Krogh's 1915 diffusion experiments to modern single-breath DLCO (H043): paired breath-hold sampling, Ogilvie & Forster's (1957) inert helium tracer dilution separating airspace mixing from true vascular uptake, Roughton & Forster's (1957) serial membrane and erythrocyte resistance model, and clinical interpretation of DLCO, VA, and KCO.

episodes.label: How the ECG Learned to Follow You Home — Waller's 1887 Limb Recordings, Einthoven's Calibrated Quartz String Galvanometer, Holter's 1961 Portable Tape Recorder & Barrett's 2014 24-Hour vs. 14-Day Patch Comparison
episodes.notes: From bedside galvanometers to ambulatory rhythm monitoring (H041): Waller's (1887) limb-contact control ruling out mechanical chest movement, Einthoven's (1903) calibrated string galvanometer, Holter's (1961) portable battery-powered recorder, and Barrett et al.'s (2014) paired 146-patient comparison showing why the adhesive patch's diagnostic advantage over 24-hour Holter monitoring (96 vs. 61) came from extended sampling duration rather than Day-1 superiority (52 vs. 61).

episodes.label: How an Audiogram Finds Which Ear Heard the Tone — Fletcher & Wegel's 1922 Calibrated Thresholds, Transcranial Bone-Conduction Crossover, Denes & Naunton's Narrowband Noise & Hood's 1957 Masking Plateau
episodes.notes: Acoustics and clinical logic of pure-tone audiometry and contralateral masking (H050): Fletcher & Wegel's (1922) calibrated receiver thresholds, skull-vibration crossover to the non-test cochlea, Denes & Naunton's (1952) frequency-band masking efficiency, and J.D. Hood's (1957) plateau method separating cross-heard responses from true ear-specific air- and bone-conduction thresholds.

episodes.label: How a Blood Test Tracks the Insulin Your Body Makes — Berson & Yalow's 1956–1960 Competitive 131I-Insulin Radioimmunoassay, Melani's 1970 Serum C-Peptide Separation & Modern Two-Antibody Electrochemiluminescence
episodes.notes: How an unexpected antibody artifact became the foundation of clinical endocrinology: Berson & Yalow's (1956-1960) competitive radioimmunoassay (where rising unlabeled hormone lowers the bound-to-free tracer ratio), Melani, Rubenstein & Steiner's (1970) detection of equimolar co-secreted C-peptide in human serum, and modern two-antibody electrochemiluminescent C-peptide testing in insulin-treated patients.

episodes.label: How a Sea Slug Gets Used to a Touch — Pinsker's Aplysia Gill-Withdrawal Habituation, Castellucci & Kandel's 1974 Quantal Failure Analysis & Bailey & Chen's Electron-Microscopy Presynaptic Active Zones
episodes.notes: From behavioral habituation to synaptic quantal release and ultrastructure in Aplysia: Pinsker et al.'s (1970) gill-withdrawal habituation and dishabituation, Castellucci & Kandel's (1974) quantal variance/failure proof that short-term habituation reflects fewer transmitter packets released per impulse rather than smaller postsynaptic unit responses, and Bailey & Chen's (1983) electron microscopy of long-term habituated sensory-neuron varicosities.

episodes.label: When the Same Taste Signal Leads to Opposite Choices — Chandrashekar's Dish Bitter Receptor Screen, Zhao & Mueller's RASSL Spiradoline Routing & Human TAS2R16 Expressed in Mouse Sweet vs. Bitter Cells
episodes.notes: Labeled-line coding in mammalian taste: separating molecular ligand detection in heterologous cells (Chandrashekar et al. 2000; Bufe et al. 2002 TAS2R16) from behavioral attraction vs. aversion in mice when the exact same engineered receptor (spiradoline RASSL, Zhao 2003) or human bitter receptor (TAS2R16, Mueller 2005) is expressed in T1R2 sweet cells vs. T2R bitter cells.

episodes.label: How a Blood Vessel Tells Itself to Relax — Furchgott & Zawadzki's 1980 Intact vs. Rubbed Rabbit Aorta, Rubanyi's Donor-Detector Perfusion, Palmer & Moncada's Ozone Chemiluminescence Nitric Oxide Proof & 15N-Arginine Tracing
episodes.notes: How the vascular endothelium's relaxing signal was identified as nitric oxide: Furchgott & Zawadzki's (1980) discovery that removing the inner endothelial lining abolishes acetylcholine relaxation while preserving smooth-muscle contraction, Rubanyi et al.'s (1985) upstream donor/downstream denuded detector bioassay, Palmer, Ferrige & Moncada's (1987) chemiluminescent nitric oxide measurement alongside Ignarro's cGMP comparison, and 15N-arginine precursor tracing.

episodes.label: How a Cell Detects an Energy Shortfall — Carling & Hardie's Shared ACC/HMG-CoA Reductase Kinase (AMPK), Hawley's Thr172 & LKB1–STRAD–MO25 Complex, Sanders's PP2Cα Protection & Gowans's AMP vs. ADP Allostery
episodes.notes: Dissecting the eukaryotic energy sensor AMPK: Carling, Zammit & Hardie's (1987) discovery that a single AMP-responsive kinase inhibits both fatty-acid and sterol synthesis, Hawley et al.'s identification of Thr172 phosphorylation by LKB1–STRAD–MO25, Sanders et al.'s (2007) cell-free proof that AMP binding shields Thr172 from dephosphorylation, and Gowans et al.'s (2013) separation of ADP/AMP protection from AMP allosteric catalysis.

episodes.label: Why a Fly's Eye Went Quiet in the Light — Cosens & Manning's 1969 Drosophila trp Mutant, Montell's Gene Rescue, Hardie & Minke's Ca2+-Selective Current, Niemeyer's trp/trpl Double Mutant & Asp621 Pore Selectivity
episodes.notes: Discovery of the founding TRP ion channel in Drosophila vision: Cosens & Manning's (1969) transient receptor potential mutant fading in continuous light, Montell & Rubin's gene rescue and cloning, Hardie & Minke's (1992) single-photoreceptor patch-clamp proof of missing Ca2+ permeability, Niemeyer et al.'s (1996) trp/trpl dissection, and Liu et al.'s (2007) pore-selectivity mutagenesis.

episodes.label: How a Cell Opens Its Own Calcium Store — Streb, Irvine, Berridge & Schulz's 1983 Permeabilized Acinar IP3 Release, Ferris's Purified IP3 Receptor Lipid Vesicles & Callamaras's Confocal Puffs-to-Waves
episodes.notes: How second-messenger calcium mobilization from internal stores was proven step by step: Streb, Irvine, Berridge & Schulz (1983) IP3-triggered Ca2+ release in permeabilized pancreatic acinar cells, Ferris et al. (1989) reconstitution of purified IP3 receptor into artificial lipid vesicles proving one protein both binds IP3 and forms the Ca2+ channel, and Callamaras et al. (1998) optical flash-photolysis puffs and waves.

episodes.label: How the End of a Pathway Slows the Beginning — Yates & Pardee's Pyrimidine Feedback, Gerhart & Schachman's Dissociated Catalytic vs. Regulatory ATCase Subunits & the 1965 MWC Allosteric Model
episodes.notes: Birth of molecular allostery: from Yates & Pardee's (1956) pyrimidine end-product inhibition in E. coli to Gerhart & Pardee's (1962) heat-desensitized aspartate transcarbamoylase (ATCase), Gerhart & Schachman's (1965) separation and reassembly of catalytic and regulatory subunits, and the Monod-Wyman-Changeux (1965) conformational equilibrium model.

episodes.label: How a Locust Turns Sound into Current — Michelsen's Abdominal Frequency Tuning, Windmill's Laser-Scanned Tympanum Waves, Warren's Auditory Receptor Currents & Chaiyasitdhi's 2-µm Axial Pull vs. Push
episodes.notes: Biophysics of insect tympanal hearing in the desert locust: Michelsen's (1968) receptor frequency tuning, Windmill et al.'s (2008) laser-vibrometry frequency-sorting waves across the abdominal tympanum, Warren & Matheson's (2018) isolated transduction currents, and Chaiyasitdhi et al.'s (2025 reviewed preprint) direct 2-µm cap pull vs. push recordings.

episodes.label: How Scientists Found a Cycle in Cell Respiration — Krebs & Johnson's 1937 Pigeon-Breast Oxygen Flasks (342 to 1,385 µL), Malonate Succinate Trapping Under O2 vs. N2 & Stern-Ochoa Condensing Enzyme
episodes.notes: How Krebs & Johnson (1937) proved cell respiration runs in a catalytic cycle rather than a linear chain: super-additive oxygen uptake with trace citrate in minced pigeon breast muscle, malonate blockade trapping succinate forward from citrate and oxaloacetate under oxygen, citrate resynthesis from oxaloacetate, and Stern, Ochoa & Lynen's (1951-1952) purified citrate synthase step.

episodes.label: How a Cell Builds Insulin from One Chain — Sanger's Two-Chain Disulfide Puzzle, Steiner & Oyer's 1967 Human Islet Tumor Pulse-Chase Proinsulin Precursor & Equimolar C-Peptide Secretion
episodes.notes: Discovery of prohormone processing: why isolated insulin A and B chains recombine inefficiently in vitro, Steiner & Oyer (1967) identification of single-chain proinsulin in human islet-cell adenoma slices, pulse-chase proof of intracellular proteolytic conversion into two-chain insulin, and Rubenstein, Clark & Steiner (1969) equimolar C-peptide co-secretion enabling clinical distinction between endogenous and exogenous insulin.

episodes.label: How You Know Where Your Hand Is in the Dark — Goodwin's 100 Hz Tendon-Vibration Illusion, Ghez's Multi-Joint Reaching Without Proprioception, Woo's Piezo2 Spindles & Chesler's Human PIEZO2 Loss
episodes.notes: From psychophysical illusions to the molecular mechanosensor of proprioception: Goodwin, McCloskey & Matthews (1972) tendon-vibration muscle-spindle illusions, Ghez et al. (1995) intersegmental dynamics defects in deafferented human reaching rescued partially by vision, Woo et al. (2015) conditional Piezo2 ablation silencing muscle-spindle Ia afferents, and Chesler et al. (2016) human PIEZO2 deficiency.

episodes.label: How Scientists Saw ATP Synthase Turn — Abrahams & Walker's Asymmetric F1 Crystal States, Noji & Yoshida's Spinning Actin Filament (120° Steps) & Itoh's Magnetic-Bead Mechanical ATP Synthesis
episodes.notes: Direct proof of rotary catalysis in F1-ATPase: Abrahams et al. (1994) 2.8 Å crystal snapshot of three distinct catalytic β conformations around an asymmetric γ axle, Noji et al. (1997) single-molecule fluorescence microscopy of unidirectional counterclockwise γ rotation and Yasuda et al. (1998) discrete 120° steps, and Itoh et al. (2004) electromagnet-driven clockwise rotation forcing net ATP synthesis.

episodes.label: How Cells Tie Growth to Available Nutrients — Heitman & Hall's Yeast FPR1/TOR1/TOR2 Rapamycin Mutants, Sabatini & Brown's Mammalian mTOR Affinity Capture & Hara's Amino-Acid Withdrawal Gate
episodes.notes: Discovery of the TOR nutrient-sensing pathway: Heitman, Movva & Hall (1991) genetic screen in Saccharomyces cerevisiae showing rapamycin requires FKBP12 (FPR1) to inhibit TOR1/TOR2, Sabatini et al. (1994) & Brown et al. (1994) biochemical capture of the ~289 kDa mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) only when rapamycin is bound to FKBP12, Barbet et al. (1996) starvation-like translation arrest, and Hara et al. (1998) amino-acid gating of insulin-stimulated p70S6K phosphorylation.

episodes.label: How a Sour Taste Starts — Huang's PKD2L1 Sour-Cell Ablation, Chang's Apical Proton Current, Tu's Otop1 Proton Channel Cloning & Teng/Zhang's Chorda Tympani Nerve Loss in Otop1-/- Mice
episodes.notes: From cell-type ablation to the molecular proton sensor for sour taste: Huang et al. (2006) selective elimination of PKD2L1 taste cells erasing chorda tympani acid responses while sparing sweet, salty, bitter, and umami, Chang, Waters & Liman (2010) direct measurement of apical proton entry, Tu et al. (2018) discovery of the OTOP1 proton channel, and Teng et al. / Zhang et al. (2019) in vivo Otop1-/- requirement for sour nerve signaling.

episodes.label: How a Cell Pumps Ions Uphill — Skou's 1957 Crab-Nerve Na++K+-Synergistic ATPase, Post's Phosphoenzyme Intermediate, Garrahan & Glynn's 3 Na+:2 K+:1 ATP Stoichiometry & Goldin's Inside-Out Vesicles
episodes.notes: Enzymology and vectorial reconstitution of the sodium-potassium pump: Skou (1957) discovery of the Mg2+/Na+/K+-activated ATPase in Carcinus maenas nerve membranes, Post, Sen & Rosenthal (1965) acyl-phosphate intermediate formed with Na+ and hydrolyzed with K+, Garrahan & Glynn (1967) 3 Na+ : 2 K+ : 1 ATP coupling ratio in resealed red-cell ghosts, and Goldin (1977) inside-out liposome reconstitution.

episodes.label: How a Cell Senses Low Oxygen — Semenza's EPO 3' Enhancer & HIF-1α/β Purification, Maxwell's VHL Ubiquitin-Tagged Normoxic Degradation & Ivan/Jaakkola's Pro564 Oxygen-Dependent Hydroxylation
episodes.notes: Molecular mechanism of cellular oxygen sensing: Semenza et al. (1991) & Wang et al. (1995) identification of the hypoxia-response element and HIF-1α/ARNT heterodimer, Maxwell et al. (1999) proof that pVHL targets HIF-α for oxygen-dependent ubiquitylation and proteasomal destruction, and Ivan et al. (2001) & Jaakkola et al. (2001) discovery of enzymatic Pro564 4-hydroxylation as the direct oxygen switch.

episodes.label: When the Lips Change the Sound You Hear — Sumby & Pollack's Speech-in-Noise Gain, McGurk & MacDonald's Ba/Ga→Da Fusion & Beauchamp's Superior Temporal Sulcus TMS Disruption
episodes.notes: Multisensory speech integration and causal cortical testing: Sumby & Pollack (1954) audiovisual enhancement in noise across vocabulary set sizes, McGurk & MacDonald (1976) cross-modal syllable fusion where auditory /ba/ paired with lip-articulated /ga/ yields heard /da/, and Beauchamp, Nath & Pasalar (2010) fMRI-guided TMS over the superior temporal sulcus selectively reducing McGurk fusion while sparing congruent control syllables.

episodes.label: How a Cell Passes a Message Inside — Sutherland & Rall's Broken-Cell Liver Homogenate Fractionation, Heat-Stable Cyclic AMP Transfer & Walsh's cAMP-Dependent Protein Kinase
episodes.notes: Discovery of the second-messenger principle: Rall, Sutherland & Berthet (1957) two-stage cell-free assay separating particulate membrane hormone response from soluble phosphorylase activation via a dialyzable, heat-stable factor, Sutherland & Rall (1958) chemical identification of cyclic 3',5'-AMP, and Walsh, Perkins & Krebs (1968) discovery of cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA).

episodes.label: How Scientists Followed Carbon Through a Tumor — Warburg's 1927 Artery-Vein Lactate Balance, DeBerardinis's 13C NMR Glioblastoma TCA & Glutaminolysis & Hensley's Intraoperative Lung Tumor Infusions
episodes.notes: From the classical Warburg Effect to human intraoperative stable-isotope tracing: Warburg, Wind & Negelein (1927) aerobic glycolysis across rat tumor vessels, DeBerardinis et al. (2007) 13C NMR isotopomer resolution of simultaneous glycolysis, TCA flux, fatty acid synthesis, and glutamine anaplerosis in glioblastoma cells, and Hensley et al. (2016) intraoperative [U-13C]glucose infusions in human NSCLC patients.

episodes.label: Why an Aroma Can Seem to Come from Your Mouth — Rozin's Dual-Olfaction Juice Test, Dalton's Subthreshold Saccharin-Benzaldehyde Integration, Small's Retronasal fMRI & Blankenship's Optogenetics
episodes.notes: Neurobiology of retronasal olfaction and flavor referral: Rozin (1982) dual-sense hypothesis, Dalton et al. (2000) subthreshold benzaldehyde + saccharin integration (28% lower threshold vs. null MSG control), Small et al. (2005) nasal-cannula fMRI showing route-dependent brain activation for identical vapor concentrations, and Blankenship et al. (2019) gustatory cortex requirement for rapid retronasal learning.

episodes.label: How a Potassium Channel Chooses an Ion — Bezanilla & Armstrong's Squid Axon Na+ Block, Heginbotham's TVGYG Signature Mutations & Doyle & MacKinnon's KcsA Selectivity Filter
episodes.notes: Atomic solution to the potassium channel selectivity paradox: Bezanilla & Armstrong (1972) >10:1 K+/Na+ selectivity and internal Na+ block in perfused squid axons, Heginbotham et al. (1994) TVGYG pore-loop mutagenesis converting a K+-selective pore into a nonselective cation channel, Doyle et al. (1998) & Zhou et al. (2001) 2.0 Å KcsA crystal structures showing backbone carbonyl cages matching dehydrated K+, and Thompson et al. (2009) planar Na+ binding.

episodes.label: How a Burst Leaves a Synapse Stronger — Bliss & Lømo's 1973 Perforant-Path LTP Controls, Collingridge's APV NMDA Blockade & Tsien's CA1-Restricted NR1 Knockout
episodes.notes: Experimental dissection of hippocampal Long-Term Potentiation (LTP): Bliss & Lømo (1973) pathway-specific potentiation lasting hours in rabbit dentate gyrus, Collingridge, Kehl & McLennan (1983) selective NMDA antagonist APV blocking LTP induction while sparing baseline AMPA synaptic transmission, and Tsien, Huerta & Tonegawa (1996) postnatal CA1 NR1 knockout mice.

episodes.label: How a Robin Reads the Tilt of a Magnetic Field — Wiltschko's 1972 Horizontal vs. Vertical Coil Flips, Ritz's Radio-Frequency Disruption & Xu's European Robin Cryptochrome 4
episodes.notes: Biophysics of the avian inclination compass: Wiltschko & Wiltschko (1972) proof that European robins read magnetic field line dip angle (poleward vs. equatorward) rather than polarity, Ritz et al. (2004) diagnostic radio-frequency spin resonance disruption, and Xu et al. (2021) transient absorption spectroscopy of purified migratory European robin vs. non-migratory chicken/pigeon Cryptochrome 4.

episodes.label: How Scientists Recorded a Single Ion Channel — Katz & Miledi's Acetylcholine Noise Variance, Neher & Sakmann's 1976 Frog Muscle Pipette Steps & Hamill's Gigaseal Configurations
episodes.notes: From statistical fluctuation analysis to direct single-molecule electrophysiology: Katz & Miledi (1972) inferring elementary acetylcholine events from voltage noise, Neher & Sakmann (1976) resolving discrete ~2.2 pA square current steps across a micro-patch of denervated frog muscle, and Hamill et al. (1981) gigaohm glass-membrane seals enabling cell-attached, whole-cell, inside-out, and outside-out configurations.

episodes.label: How a Cell Builds a Droplet in the Right Place — C. elegans P Granules, Brangwynne's Shear-Induced Dripping & FRAP Recovery, MEX-5 Gradient Dissolution & MEG-3 Scaffolding
episodes.notes: Discovery of intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation: Hird et al. (1996) live GFP::PIE-1 imaging of C. elegans P granules, Brangwynne et al. (2009) proof of liquid wetting, fusion, ~second FRAP exchange, and spatial condensation/dissolution asymmetry, and Smith et al. (2016) & Folkmann et al. (2021) MEX-5 RNA competition and intrinsically disordered MEG-3 surface clusters.

episodes.label: When the Same Sound Becomes a Surprise — Sutton's P300 Uncertainty Cue, Bekinschtein's Local-vs.-Global Oddball Hierarchy & Wacongne's Omitted-Tone Prediction Error
episodes.notes: Electrophysiology of auditory expectation and hierarchical prediction error: Sutton et al. (1965) P300 discovery comparing identical clicks under certainty vs. uncertainty, Bekinschtein et al. (2009) local-global paradigm where a locally Deviant XXXXX/XXXXY sequence becomes the global rule, and Wacongne et al. (2011) brain responses to an omitted expected tone.

episodes.label: How Light Sets the Body Clock — Rodless/Coneless Circadian Phase Shifts, Berson's Retrograde SCN Ganglion Cells, Melanopsin Knockout Rescue & Opn4Diphtheria Ablation
episodes.notes: Discovery of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs): Freedman et al. (1999) intact circadian photoentrainment without rods and cones, Berson, Dunn & Takao (2002) intrinsic light responses in SCN-projecting ganglion cells after synaptic isolation, Hattar et al. (2003) triple-knockout loss of entrainment when rods, cones, and melanopsin are removed together, and Güler et al. (2008) ipRGC cell ablation.

episodes.label: How Infants Tune In to Speech — Werker & Tees's 6-to-12-Month Head-Turn Narrowing, Maye's Bimodal vs. Unimodal Distributions, Kuhl's Live-vs.-Video Mandarin & Lytle's Peer Contingency
episodes.notes: Perceptual narrowing in infant speech acquisition: Werker & Tees (1984) preservation of English contrasts alongside loss of non-native Hindi/Salish discrimination by 10–12 months, Maye, Werker & Gerken (2002) statistical bimodal vs. unimodal distribution reshaping, Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003) live vs. televised Mandarin tutors, and Lytle, Garcia-Sierra & Kuhl (2018) peer-paired contingent video.

episodes.label: A Sodium Channel for Pain and Smell — Cox's SCN9A (NaV1.7) Nonsense Variants, Patch-Clamp Loss of Current & Weiss's Olfactory Glomerular Synaptic Failure
episodes.notes: How one voltage-gated sodium channel links nociception and olfaction: Cox et al. (2006) biallelic SCN9A (NaV1.7) truncations eliminating pain while sparing touch, and Weiss et al. (2011) dual recordings proving NaV1.7-null olfactory sensory neurons fire odor-evoked action potentials at the soma but fail to trigger synaptic transmission in the olfactory bulb glomerulus.

episodes.label: What an Eye Movement Can Tell Us About Dreaming — Aserinsky & Kleitman's 1953 EOG Awakenings, Dement's Duration Judgments, Foulkes's Definition Shift & Siclari's Posterior Hot Zone
episodes.notes: From Aserinsky & Kleitman's (1953) discovery of Rapid Eye Movement sleep and Dement & Kleitman's (1957) 5-vs.-15-minute binary duration judgments to Foulkes's (1962) proof that NREM mental activity depends on definition thresholds and Siclari et al.'s (2017) posterior cortical low-frequency reduction predicting dream experience within both REM and NREM sleep.

episodes.label: The Mirror-Image Test for an Opioid Receptor — Goldstein's Stereospecificity, Pert & Snyder's [3H]Naloxone Levorphanol vs. Dextrorphan Assay & Enkephalin Discovery
episodes.notes: Biochemical proof of brain opioid receptors: Goldstein et al. (1971) enantiomeric competition concept, Pert & Snyder (1973) [3H]naloxone vacuum-filtration assay showing stereospecific displacement by (-)-levorphanol but not (+)-dextrorphan, Hughes et al. (1975) discovery of endogenous pentapeptides Met- and Leu-enkephalin, and 1992 delta-receptor cloning.

episodes.label: How the Nose Builds an Odor Code — Buck & Axel's Olfactory Receptor Family, Zhao's Adenoviral I7 Pairing, Malnic's Combinatorial Code & Bozza's Bulb Glomeruli
episodes.notes: Molecular logic of combinatorial olfaction: Buck & Axel (1991) cloning of the odorant receptor superfamily, Zhao et al. (1998) functional pairing of receptor I7 with octanal, Malnic et al. (1999) single-neuron calcium imaging + RT-PCR showing concentration-dependent recruitment (2 to 5 to 8 receptors for bromooctanoic acid), and Bozza et al. (2004) in vivo glomerular synapto-pHluorin maps.

episodes.label: How the Ear Turns Up Its Own Volume — Brownell's Outer Hair Cell Electromotility, Zheng's Prestin Discovery & Dallos's Stiffness-Preserving Knock-In
episodes.notes: Biophysics of the cochlear amplifier: Brownell et al. (1985) voltage-driven length changes in guinea-pig outer hair cells, Zheng et al. (2000) subtractive cloning of prestin (SLC26A5), Liberman et al. (2002) 40–60 dB threshold shift in prestin-/- mice, and Dallos et al. (2008) 499-prestin knock-in separating active motor force from passive axial stiffness.

episodes.label: Why a Chili Pepper Feels Hot — Caterina & Julius's TRPV1 Expression-Cloning Screen, Thermal Activation, Knockout Hyperalgesia & Chicken-Rat Chimeras
episodes.notes: Discovery and dissection of polymodal nociception via TRPV1: Caterina et al. (1997) Fura-2 expression cloning from dorsal root ganglia, physical heat (>43°C) gating of the capsaicin receptor, Caterina et al. (2000) TRPV1-/- loss of inflammatory thermal hyperalgesia, and Jordt & Julius (2002) separation of capsaicin and thermal gating in avian-mammalian chimeras.

episodes.label: A Chemical Signal Comes in Packets — Fatt & Katz Miniature Endplate Potentials, Del Castillo & Katz Poisson Quantal Failures & Heuser-Reese Quick-Freeze Exocytosis
episodes.notes: Statistical and ultrastructural proof of quantal synaptic transmission: Fatt & Katz (1952) spontaneous miniature endplate potentials, del Castillo & Katz (1954) independent quantal content estimates (0.57 by amplitude ratio vs. 0.56 by Poisson failure fraction), and Heuser & Reese (1979) 3–5 ms quick-freeze electron microscopy.

episodes.label: How a Shark Finds a Fish Under Sand — Murray's Ampullae of Lorenzini Recordings, Kalmijn's Agar-Chamber & Dipole Strikes & Sawfish Electrosense
episodes.notes: Experimental proof of passive electroreception in elasmobranchs: Murray (1962) ampullae of Lorenzini nerve recordings, Kalmijn (1971) catshark and skate strikes at agar-screened live plaice vs. polyethylene insulation vs. artificial bioelectric dipoles, and Wueringer et al. (2012) sawfish rostral electrosense.

episodes.notes: Ionic basis of GABAergic polarity switches: Rivera et al. (1999) KCC2 antisense knockdown in hippocampal neurons, Coull et al. (2003, 2005) gramicidin-perforated patch recordings in spinal lamina I after nerve injury (-72.6 mV to -49.0 mV) driven by microglial BDNF-TrkB signaling, and depolarizing shunting conductance.

episodes.notes: Neuroethology of the monarch butterfly time-compensated sun compass: Mouritsen & Frost (2002) ±6h photoperiod shifts (225° vs. 136° vs. 335°), Merlin et al. (2009) antennal light-entrained circadian oscillators, and Guerra et al. (2012) rescue of group orientation by amputating a desynchronized black-painted antenna.

episodes.notes: Synaptic competition and critical period closure in visual cortex: Wiesel & Hubel (1963–1970) why monocular suture shifts cortical drive (1/84 cells) while binocular suture preserves responsiveness, and Pizzorusso et al. (2002) extracellular matrix chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan digestion in adult rats.

(1970) porcine secretin purification, and Ishihara et al. (1991) secretin receptor cAMP signaling.

episodes.notes: Decisive experimental tests of chemiosmotic coupling: Mitchell (1961), Jagendorf & Uribe (1966) spinach thylakoid acid-bath pH jump (141 vs. 12 nmol ATP/mg chlorophyll in darkness), and Racker & Stoeckenius (1974) halobacterial bacteriorhodopsin + bovine mitochondrial ATP synthase proteoliposomes.

episodes.notes: Experimental discovery of bat echolocation: Pierce & Griffin (1938) ultrasonic heterodyne detector, Griffin & Galambos (1941) reversible sight vs. hearing vs. vocalization blocks, terminal buzz pursuit (1960), and Kick & Simmons (1984) electronic delay-line phantom targets.

episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology & Forensic Toxicology of cocaine: why urine immunoassays detect hydrolytic metabolite benzoylecgonine for days after parent cocaine (T1/2 ~1h) has cleared, Nielsen et al.'s (2024) 2.66 Å cryo-EM structure of human DAT bound to cocaine (PDB 9EO4), hepatic carboxylesterase transesterification with ethanol to form long-acting cocaethylene, serial hs-cTnI rule-in, and Lange et al.'s (1989, 1990) coronary catheterization proof of alpha-adrenergic vasospasm.

episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of ondansetron and biphasic chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting: Cubeddu & Marty's 1990 cisplatin trials, 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure of 5-HT3A bound to ondansetron (PDB 6W1M), why acute (0–24h) peripheral 5-HT3 vagal signaling gives way to delayed (24–120h) central NK1/Substance P signaling, hERG K+ channel blockade and FDA IV dose caps, and CPIC CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer guidance.

episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of baclofen neurotoxicity in renal impairment: Keberle's 1962 lipophilic GABA design and Bowery's 1980 GABAB receptor discovery, human GABAB1-GABAB2 heterodimer crystal/cryo-EM structures (PDB 4MS4, 7EB2), why 69–85% unchanged renal clearance causes rapid accumulation, triphasic/burst-suppression encephalopathy, and coma in CKD (Muanda et al. 2019), and EXTRIP guideline criteria for emergent hemodialysis.

episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of intrathecal ziconotide (PRIALT / omega-conotoxin MVIIA): Olivera's discovery of Conus magus peptide toxins, Nieng Yan's 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of human CaV2.2 plugged by ziconotide (PDB 7MIX), why systemic IV delivery causes orthostatic hypotension via sympathetic CaV2.2 block while intrathecal delivery targets dorsal horn lamina I/II synapses without tolerance or respiratory depression, and Staats (2004) vs. Rauck (2006) titration kinetics.

episodes.label: The Vitamin the Body Couldn't Clear — PTH-Suppressed Hypercalcemia, Human VDR-Calcitriol Structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann's LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D:24,25(OH)2D Ratio & CYP24A1 Loss
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of vitamin D catabolism and CYP24A1 deficiency: why normal 25(OH)D3 with suppressed PTH and elevated 1,25(OH)2D3 points to failed 24-hydroxylase inactivation rather than overdose, the 1.8 Å human VDR-calcitriol crystal structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann & Jones's (2014) PTAD-derivatized LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D3:24,25(OH)2D3 molar ratio diagnostic (>80), and Schlingmann et al.'s (2011) discovery of idiopathic infantile and adult CYP24A1 hypercalcemia.

episodes.label: The First Breath Caffeine Bought — Apnea of Prematurity, Aranda's 1977 Trial, Human A2A Receptor Cryo-EM/X-Ray (PDB 5MZP/5G53), CYP1A2 Ontogeny & CAP Trial Outcomes
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of caffeine citrate in apnea of prematurity: central vs. obstructive vs. mixed apnea traces, Aranda et al. (1977) and Murat et al. (1981) clinical trials, human A2A receptor crystal structures (PDB 5MZP, 5G53) showing competitive adenosine blockade, neonatal CYP1A2 ontogeny (~100-hour T1/2 vs. 4–6 hours in adults) and 2:1 salt-to-base dosing safety, and the 2,006-infant CAP trial through age 11 (Schmidt et al. 2006, 2007, 2017).

episodes.label: The Aspirin That Changed the Breathing — Hoffmann's Acetylsalicylic Acid, Vane's Prostaglandin Blockade & Human COX-2 Ser530 Acetylation (5F19 vs. 5F1A), Mitochondrial Uncoupling, Chloride Electrode Artifacts & EXTRIP Dialysis
episodes.notes: Covalent enzyme acetylation meets clinical toxicology: Hoffmann's 1900 aspirin patent, Vane and Smith & Willis's 1971 prostaglandin inhibition, Roth's irreversible platelet COX acetylation, and Lucido's human COX-2 crystal structures (acetylated Ser530 in PDB 5F19 vs. salicylate-bound 5F1A), paired with a serial salicylate poisoning timeline showing mixed respiratory alkalosis and high-anion-gap acidosis, salicylate-induced chloride ISE pseudohyperchloremia, mitochondrial protonophoric uncoupling, pH-dependent nonionized CNS entry, and EXTRIP hemodialysis criteria.

episodes.label: The Sugar That Stayed in the Scan — [18F]FDG from 1976–1979 Brain Autoradiography (Sokoloff & Reivich) and Cyclotron 109.77-Min Decay to GLUT3/Hexokinase II Trapping (4ZW9/2NZT), Thoracic SUVmax 7.2 & EBUS Granulomas
episodes.notes: From cyclotron target to thoracic staging needle: Sokoloff's 1977 [14C]deoxyglucose method and Reivich/Alavi/Phelps's 1976-1979 human [18F]FDG brain studies, Hamacher nucleophilic synthesis and 109.77-minute half-life batch logistics (21 CFR 212.70), D-glucose-bound GLUT3 (PDB 4ZW9) and human hexokinase II (PDB 2NZT) metabolic trapping, 511-keV coincidence physics and SUVbw math (7.2 g/mL), and why bilateral FDG-avid mediastinal nodes still require EBUS-TBNA tissue confirmation (granulomatous inflammation vs. metastasis).

episodes.notes: Two ward records seventy years apart: chlorpromazine's transition from Rhône-Poulenc synthesis (US2645640A) and Laborit's 1952 surgical 'artificial hibernation' to Delay & Deniker's psychiatric cases, Elkes & Elkes's 1954 crossover, and the 1964 NIMH Collaborative Study, paired with a contemporary pause-triggered torsades workup (Fridericia QTc 531 ms), ligand-free human hERG cryo-EM (PDB 5VA1), oocyte vs. CHO IC50s (21.6 vs. 1.47 µM), and DRD2 residence kinetics.

episodes.notes: Separating body-composition compartments, individual muscle hypertrophy, and glycemic tolerance when dietary protein meets resistance load: Trautman et al.'s (2023) 2x2 mouse amino-acid/weight-pulling factorial (protecting against fat accretion while leaving high-protein glucose intolerance unchanged, P=0.7442), Sestrin2–leucine and GATOR2 structural mechanics, Drummond's human rapamycin biopsy tracer study, and Longland (2016) vs. Layman (2005) human trials.

(2020) 12-human heat-exercise soft-drink crossover, García-Arroyo et al. (2017) Wistar rat V1a/V2 conivaptan blockade, and Tourula et al. (2026) hypotonic vs. hypertonic sports drinks.

episodes.label: The Glucose That Couldn't Leave the Liver — Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia, ER G6PC1 His176 Phosphohistidine Catalysis vs. SLC37A4, Uncooked Cornstarch & DTX401 Gene Therapy
episodes.notes: From acute fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis in glycogen storage disease type Ia to ER lumenal G6PC1 His176 phosphohistidine hydrolysis vs. SLC37A4 glucose-6-phosphate transport, Grefhorst's ChREBP/LXRalpha mouse blockade vs. human [6,6-2H2]glucose flux, uncooked cornstarch therapy, and AAV8 G6PC1 gene replacement.

episodes.label: The Sugar That Stayed After the Milk Was Gone — Classic Galactosemia, GALT Ping-Pong His186 Catalysis (5IN3), Endogenous [1-13C]Galactose Production & Aldose Reductase
episodes.notes: Why lifelong dietary galactose restriction saves neonates from acute hepatorenal crisis yet fails to prevent long-term speech and ovarian complications in classic galactosemia: human GALT double-displacement His186 uridylylation (PDB 5IN3), Berry et al. [1-13C]galactose isotope-dilution proof of ~1 g/day endogenous galactose synthesis, and aldose reductase galactitol reduction.

episodes.label: The Hormone That Heard Less Protein — Dietary Protein Restriction, Hepatocyte FGF21 Induction, Beta-Klotho 5VAQ Docking, FAP Cleavage & Intact vs. Total ELISA
episodes.notes: Endocrine and structural dissection of human FGF21 induction during low-protein and sucrose feeding (Nicolaisen, Ramne, Laeger): C-terminal beta-Klotho docking (PDB 5VAQ), fibroblast activation protein (FAP) Pro171 cleavage separating intact bioactive FGF21 from total immunoreactive FGF21, and central Klb macronutrient preference circuits.

episodes.label: The Leucine That Wouldn’t Clear — Maple Syrup Urine Disease, BCKDH E1 Phosphorylation (1DTW/1OLS), Isobaric LC-MS/MS Alloisoleucine & Liver Transplant Flux
episodes.notes: Biochemical and analytical dissection of Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD) decompensation: human BCKDH E1 alpha-ketoacid decarboxylation and BCKDK Ser292 phosphorylation (PDB 1DTW/1OLS/4H7Q), chromatographic separation of isobaric leucine, isoleucine, alloisoleucine, and hydroxyproline at m/z 132->86, LAT1 blood-brain barrier competition, IV BCAA-free rescue, and liver transplantation.

episodes.label: The First Calories Back — Refeeding Syndrome, Insulin-Driven Phosphate/Potassium Shifts, PDH E1 ThDP Geometry (1NI4) & Doig ICU Trial
episodes.notes: From starvation to refeeding syndrome in the ICU: insulin-stimulated Na+/K+-ATPase potassium uptake and intracellular phosphate trapping, human pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 thiamine diphosphate (ThDP) active-site geometry (PDB 1NI4), whole-blood ThDP LC-MS/MS assays, diaphragmatic weakness in hypophosphatemia (Aubier 1985), and the Doig et al. (2015) caloric restriction trial.

episodes.label: What the Colon Sends Back — Inulin Fermentation, Eudragit Colon-Targeted [1-13C]SCFAs, Systemic Availability (36% Acetate, 9% Propionate, 2% Butyrate) & FFAR2 8J24
episodes.notes: Atomic and clinical tracing of colonic short-chain fatty acids (Boets et al. 2015, 2017; Bloemen et al. 2009): Bacteroides ovatus inulin cleavage, Roseburia/Faecalibacterium acetate-to-butyrate cross-feeding, Eudragit S100 colon-targeted [1-13C]SCFA capsules with IV [2H]SCFA clearance calibration (36% acetate, 9.2% propionate, 2.4% butyrate systemic availability), and human FFAR2 cryo-EM (PDB 8J24).

episodes.label: Three Roads to Liver Fat — Chylomicron NEFA Spillover, Multi-Tracer Liver Biopsies, Human FASN 9MJ9 & Beverage De Novo Lipogenesis
episodes.notes: Quantitative isotope dissection of hepatic triacylglycerol sources across three human studies: Piché et al. (2018) chylomicron-derived [U-13C]palmitate spillover, Donnelly et al. (2005) 4-day triple-tracer liver biopsies (59% NEFA, 26% DNL, 15% dietary within accounted fraction), human FASN cryo-EM (PDB 9MJ9), and Geidl-Flueck et al. (2021) sugar-sweetened beverage VLDL-palmitate secretion.

episodes.label: The Carbon in the Next Breath — [U-13C6]Fructose Meal Oxidation, KHK-A 2HW1 Active Site, GC-C-IRMS Plasma Glucose & 7T Hepatic Deuterium Imaging
episodes.notes: Stable-isotope tracing of ingested [U-13C6]fructose in humans (Theytaz et al. 2014): GLUT5 uptake, ketohexokinase KHK-A vs. KHK-C phosphorylation (PDB 2HW1), aldolase B cleavage, GC-C-IRMS 13C-glucose and breath 13CO2 recovery, paired with 7-Tesla hepatic deuterium metabolic imaging (Brunasso et al. 2026).

episodes.label: One Ångström Under the Mucus — Human Airway Axonemal Dynein (PDB 8J07), Periciliary Brush Exclusion, DNAH5 Splice Defects & Nasal Nitric Oxide
episodes.notes: Atomic-to-clinical journey through mucociliary clearance and Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD): human airway doublet microtubule structure (Walton et al. 2023, PDB 8J07), periciliary brush osmotic exclusion (Button et al. 2012), nasal nitric oxide chemiluminescence, and DNAH5 intronic splice-site RT-PCR.

episodes.label: One Ångström When the Artery Opens — Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion, Succinate Accumulation, Complex I Reverse Electron Transport & Infarct Salvage
episodes.notes: Atomic and clinical timeline of the first minutes after coronary artery reperfusion: Jennings & Reimer's (1960/1977) canine wavefront of necrosis, coronary-sinus succinate release, Complex I flavin site reverse electron transport (RET) superoxide burst upon reoxygenation, and why ischemic postconditioning failed to reduce clinical STEMI endpoints.

episodes.label: One Ångström Through the Splenic Gate — Red Cell Interendothelial Slits, PIEZO1 Hereditary Xerocytosis (8YEZ/8YFG), Gardos KCNN4 & Ektacytometry
episodes.notes: Squeezing a human erythrocyte through a sub-micron splenic interendothelial slit: PIEZO1 mechanosensitive dome flattening and MDFIC-bound slowed inactivation (PDB 8YEZ/8YFG, 6.1 ms vs. 17.4 ms), Ca2+-activated Gardos (KCNN4) potassium/water efflux, osmotic gradient ektacytometry shifts, and why splenectomy triggers portal/thrombotic catastrophe in PIEZO1 hereditary xerocytosis.

episodes.label: One Ångström Riding the Flagellum — Sperm Capacitation, CatSper Pore Architecture (7EEB), Whole-Cell Patch Clamp & Hyperactivated Beat
episodes.notes: Atomic and electrophysiological journey along the principal piece of a sperm flagellum: mouse CatSperosome cryo-EM architecture (PDB 7EEB) vs. human cytoplasmic-droplet whole-cell patch-clamp recordings (Lishko/Strunker 2011; Mansell 2014), the 2016 ABHD2 hypothesis vs. 2026 selective inhibitor tests, and CATSPER-deficient IVF failure rescued by ICSI.

episodes.label: One Ångström Across the Gut Barrier — Enteric Translocation, TLR4–MD-2 Lipid A Dimerization (3FXI), Microvascular Shunting & Septic Shock
episodes.notes: From an injured intestinal barrier and mesenteric lymph node cultures (Deitch 1989) to the crystal structure of human TLR4-MD-2 bound to E. coli Ra LPS (PDB 3FXI), sublingual microvascular shunting (De Backer 2002), endothelial glycocalyx shedding, and why eritoran MD-2 blockade failed in the Phase III ACCESS sepsis trial.

episodes.label: One Ångström from a Dividing Cell — Paclitaxel in the β-Tubulin Taxane Pocket (1JFF), Cremophor Anaphylaxis & Mitotic Spindle Fate
episodes.notes: Atomic-scale journey into the luminal beta-tubulin taxane pocket (PDB 1JFF): distinguishing Cremophor EL complement-mediated infusion anaphylaxis from delayed neutropenia, M-loop lateral protofilament stabilization, and multipolar mitotic spindle catastrophe in human tumors.

episodes.label: How the End of a Pathway Slows the Beginning — Yates & Pardee's Pyrimidine Feedback, Gerhart & Schachman's Dissociated Catalytic vs. Regulatory ATCase Subunits & the 1965 MWC Allosteric Model
episodes.notes: Birth of molecular allostery: from Yates & Pardee's (1956) pyrimidine end-product inhibition in E. coli to Gerhart & Pardee's (1962) heat-desensitized aspartate transcarbamoylase (ATCase), Gerhart & Schachman's (1965) separation and reassembly of catalytic and regulatory subunits, and the Monod-Wyman-Changeux (1965) conformational equilibrium model.

episodes.label: How Scientists Saw ATP Synthase Turn — Abrahams & Walker's Asymmetric F1 Crystal States, Noji & Yoshida's Spinning Actin Filament (120° Steps) & Itoh's Magnetic-Bead Mechanical ATP Synthesis
episodes.notes: Direct proof of rotary catalysis in F1-ATPase: Abrahams et al. (1994) 2.8 Å crystal snapshot of three distinct catalytic β conformations around an asymmetric γ axle, Noji et al. (1997) single-molecule fluorescence microscopy of unidirectional counterclockwise γ rotation and Yasuda et al. (1998) discrete 120° steps, and Itoh et al. (2004) electromagnet-driven clockwise rotation forcing net ATP synthesis.

episodes.label: How a Cell Pumps Ions Uphill — Skou's 1957 Crab-Nerve Na++K+-Synergistic ATPase, Post's Phosphoenzyme Intermediate, Garrahan & Glynn's 3 Na+:2 K+:1 ATP Stoichiometry & Goldin's Inside-Out Vesicles
episodes.notes: Enzymology and vectorial reconstitution of the sodium-potassium pump: Skou (1957) discovery of the Mg2+/Na+/K+-activated ATPase in Carcinus maenas nerve membranes, Post, Sen & Rosenthal (1965) acyl-phosphate intermediate formed with Na+ and hydrolyzed with K+, Garrahan & Glynn (1967) 3 Na+ : 2 K+ : 1 ATP coupling ratio in resealed red-cell ghosts, and Goldin (1977) inside-out liposome reconstitution.

episodes.label: How a Cell Senses Low Oxygen — Semenza's EPO 3' Enhancer & HIF-1α/β Purification, Maxwell's VHL Ubiquitin-Tagged Normoxic Degradation & Ivan/Jaakkola's Pro564 Oxygen-Dependent Hydroxylation
episodes.notes: Molecular mechanism of cellular oxygen sensing: Semenza et al. (1991) & Wang et al. (1995) identification of the hypoxia-response element and HIF-1α/ARNT heterodimer, Maxwell et al. (1999) proof that pVHL targets HIF-α for oxygen-dependent ubiquitylation and proteasomal destruction, and Ivan et al. (2001) & Jaakkola et al. (2001) discovery of enzymatic Pro564 4-hydroxylation as the direct oxygen switch.

episodes.label: How a Potassium Channel Chooses an Ion — Bezanilla & Armstrong's Squid Axon Na+ Block, Heginbotham's TVGYG Signature Mutations & Doyle & MacKinnon's KcsA Selectivity Filter
episodes.notes: Atomic solution to the potassium channel selectivity paradox: Bezanilla & Armstrong (1972) >10:1 K+/Na+ selectivity and internal Na+ block in perfused squid axons, Heginbotham et al. (1994) TVGYG pore-loop mutagenesis converting a K+-selective pore into a nonselective cation channel, Doyle et al. (1998) & Zhou et al. (2001) 2.0 Å KcsA crystal structures showing backbone carbonyl cages matching dehydrated K+, and Thompson et al. (2009) planar Na+ binding.

episodes.label: How a Cell Builds a Droplet in the Right Place — C. elegans P Granules, Brangwynne's Shear-Induced Dripping & FRAP Recovery, MEX-5 Gradient Dissolution & MEG-3 Scaffolding
episodes.notes: Discovery of intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation: Hird et al. (1996) live GFP::PIE-1 imaging of C. elegans P granules, Brangwynne et al. (2009) proof of liquid wetting, fusion, ~second FRAP exchange, and spatial condensation/dissolution asymmetry, and Smith et al. (2016) & Folkmann et al. (2021) MEX-5 RNA competition and intrinsically disordered MEG-3 surface clusters.
